title: Cayman: Custom Accelerator Generation with Control Flow and Data Access Optimization
problem: High-level synthesis for custom accelerators requires manual kernel selection and extraction, limiting automated SoC accelerator design; existing tools lack control flow and data access optimization.
motivation: Custom accelerators enhance SoC performance but require automated kernel identification and optimization to reduce manual effort and improve design productivity.
method: Cayman analyzes the entire application using a hierarchical program representation—a structured view ranging from high-level logic down to detailed operations—to automatically identify computationally intensive sections (kernels) worth converting to hardware, even when those sections involve complex decision-making (control flow). It then optimizes the data pathways between the main processor and accelerators, and merges similar accelerators into reusable designs.
key_novelty: Cayman automatically identifies and extracts performance-critical code sections (kernels) from complete applications—including those with complex control flow—using hierarchical program analysis.
contributions: Hierarchical program representation for automatic kernel selection
Specialized processor-accelerator interface optimization for data access
Novel accelerator merging mechanism for reusability

metrics.speedup: 8.0x vs framework A, 14.4x vs framework B

primary_theme: automated end-to-end custom accelerator synthesis with control flow
